Press the shortcut key. Each button on the keyboard then shows the key that operates it: a number under each toolbar icon, a letter under each tool in the toolbox, and Shift with a key for the symbol and emoji rows.

T opens the full toolbox, and ? shows the list of every key, including the tools that are not on the screen.

The shortcut key is two presses of Ctrl by default. No app uses this, because a Ctrl alone makes no character, and the keyboard still passes it through. You can change the shortcut key and every letter below.

title: Arrow keys move a highlight
name: typing_hw_panel_nav_title
description: Arrows move a highlight in a tool, Enter selects it, Esc closes the tool
help:
In a tool, the arrow keys move a highlight over the emoji, the clips or the results. Enter uses the item with the highlight. Tab moves between the search box, the category chips and the results.

The highlight shows only after you press a key. It never shows while you use the keyboard by touch.

title: Arrow keys move over the keys
name: typing_hw_dpad_keys_title
description: A ring on one key; the centre button or Enter types it
help:
For a television remote, which has no other way to reach a key. The arrow keys move a ring from key to key and the centre button types the key it is on. Left and right stay inside the row. Up from the top row leaves the keyboard, so the remote can go back to the app.

Hold the centre button to open the alternates of the key the ring is on, then pick one with the arrows. Escape puts the ring away, so Enter goes back to the text field.

On a television this is on to begin with. Everywhere else it starts off, because the arrow keys belong to the text field you are typing in.

title: Esc closes the tool
name: typing_hw_esc_title
description: Escape closes an open tool instead of going to the app
help: Escape closes only what the keyboard has open. With no tool open, Escape goes straight to the app, so it still stops a page load or exits insert mode in an editor.

title: Ctrl + number opens a toolbar tool
name: typing_hw_digit_chord_title
description: Ctrl+1 opens the toolbox, Ctrl+2 the first tool, and so on
help:
The numbers count the buttons on the toolbar from the start. Ctrl+1 is the toolbox button, Ctrl+2 is the first tool after it. Ctrl+0 is the tenth button.

This needs no shortcut key first. Turn it off if you use Ctrl with a number in your apps: browsers and editors change tab with it, and the keyboard takes the key first while you write in a text field.

The same numbers also work after the shortcut key, at any setting.

title: Ctrl+Space changes the language
name: typing_hw_lang_chord_title
description: Hold Ctrl to browse the language list, release to switch
help:
Ctrl+Space goes to the next language and Ctrl+Shift+Space to the one before. Keep Ctrl held and press Space again to step through the list on screen. The keyboard switches when Ctrl comes back up. Esc cancels.

Some apps use Ctrl+Space themselves, for example code editors use it to show completions. While this is on, the keyboard takes the shortcut when you type in those apps. Turn it off here to give it back.

If the shortcut key that opens tools is also set to Ctrl+Space, the language switch wins. A keyboard with its own language key does not need this setting: that key always works.

title: Write the modifier names
name: typing_hw_modifier_words_title
description: Show Ctrl and Shift on the keys instead of their symbols
help:
The keys under each button read "Ctrl+2" and "Shift+Q". These are the names printed on a PC keyboard.

Turn this off for the shorter symbols. They take less space, but they come from Mac keyboards, and a keyboard that does not print them gives you no help to read them.

title: Time to press a key
name: typing_hw_picker_timeout_title
description: How long the keys stay on the screen after the shortcut key
help:
After you press the shortcut key, each button shows the key that operates it. This is how long they stay before the keyboard goes back to usual.

Make this longer while you learn the keys. Make it shorter when you know them, because the keyboard does nothing else until the time is finished or you press a key.

title: Number keys select suggestions
name: typing_hw_suggestion_hotkeys_title
description: Type a suggestion by its number in the suggestion strip
help:
You cannot press the suggestion strip while you type on a physical keyboard. A number key selects a suggestion instead.

"After the shortcut key" is the safe choice, because nothing else uses it. "Alt + number" needs one key less, but browsers, editors and chat apps use a modifier with a number to switch tabs and workspaces.

title: Show the suggestion numbers
name: typing_hw_suggestion_hints_title
description: Put the key under each suggestion while a physical keyboard is connected
help:
Each suggestion shows the key that selects it, for as long as a physical keyboard is connected.

This applies only to "Alt + number", which needs no shortcut key first. With "After the shortcut key", the numbers show after you press the shortcut key, because that is when they operate.

title: macOS shortcuts
name: typing_hw_mac_title
description: Command and Option behave as they do on a Mac
help:
For a keyboard made for a Mac. Command is the key next to the space bar.

Command+C, Command+V, Command+X and Command+A copy, paste, cut and select all. Command+Z is undo and Command+Shift+Z is redo. Command+Left and Command+Right go to the start and the end of the line. Option+Left and Option+Right move one word. Option+Backspace deletes one word, and Command+Backspace deletes to the start of the line. Hold Shift with a move to select.

Ctrl keeps its usual behaviour, and every other Command shortcut goes to the app. Some devices keep a small number of Command shortcuts for the system, and those do not reach the keyboard.

title: Show the keyboard for shortcuts
name: typing_hw_auto_show_title
description: A shortcut that opens a tool also shows the keyboard
help: With a physical keyboard, there is usually no on-screen keyboard, and a tool has no space to draw. With this setting on, a shortcut that opens a tool shows the keyboard. When you close the tool, the keyboard hides again.

title: Swipe to delete
name: typing_backspace_swipe_title
description: Swipe sideways on backspace to delete more than one press
help: Press backspace and swipe left. Each step of the swipe deletes one more word, or one more character, as you set below. A plain press, or a press and hold, still deletes one character at a time.

title: Swipe deletes
name: typing_backspace_unit_title
description: What one step of the backspace swipe takes off
help: Words clear a sentence in one pull. Characters walk back a letter at a time, which is the finer tool when you must fix the middle of a word. The distance for one step is set below, and it is a different distance for each of the two.

title: Show what you will delete
name: typing_backspace_preview_title
description: Select the text as you swipe, and delete it when you lift your finger
help: The swipe highlights the text it is about to delete instead of deleting as it goes, so you can see how far you have got. Swipe back to the right to give text back, and lift your finger to delete what is left highlighted. Turn this off to delete each word or character the moment you swipe past it.

title: Word delete distance
name: typing_backspace_step_title
description: How far you swipe backspace to delete the first word
help: Later words come off faster than the first on a fixed curve, so this one distance tunes the whole gesture. Raise it if words disappear by accident, lower it if clearing a sentence takes too long a pull. This setting is 72 dp by default.

title: Character delete distance
name: typing_backspace_char_step_title
description: How far you swipe backspace for each character
help: Every character costs the same pull, with no speed up, so the count stays easy to follow. Raise it if letters go by too quickly, lower it if a long correction takes too much room. This setting is 20 dp by default.

title: Swipe on forward delete
name: typing_forward_delete_swipe_title
description: Swipe right on the forward delete key to clear the text ahead
help:
Press the forward delete key and swipe right. Each step of the swipe deletes one more word, or one more character, ahead of the cursor. It is the backspace swipe pointed the other way, and it follows the same three settings above: what one step takes off, whether you see it first, and how far you drag for one step.

The forward delete key is not on the standard keyboard. Add it to a row, or to a key you press and hold, in the layout editor.

title: Alternate key size
name: keypress_alternates_size_title
description: Text size in the press and hold popup
help:
This multiplies the size of the characters in the popup that opens when you press and hold a key. It reaches further than the popup font size above, because the popup of alternates grows to fit whatever you put in it.

The preview bubble keeps its own size, so a large value here does not push the character out of the bubble.

title: Alternate key spacing
name: keypress_alternates_padding_title
description: Room around each character in the popup
help:
This is the space around each alternate. It sets the gap between them and the size of the area that you can tap, so raise it if you hit the wrong character.

A higher value makes the popup wider, and a wide popup wraps onto more rows.

title: Alternate key columns
name: keypress_alternates_columns_title
description: How many alternates go on one row
help:
Auto puts as many alternates on a row as fit on the screen, so the shape of the popup follows the width of the characters.

A number from 3 to 11 gives every row that many columns of the same width. A key with many alternates then reads as a block, and each alternate is in the same place each time that you open it.

title: Closest to the key first
name: keypress_alternates_nearest_title
description: Fill the popup from the key outward
help:
The popup opens above the key that you hold. This decides which end of it the first alternate goes to.

Off: the first alternate is at the top left and the popup fills downward, like lines of text. On a popup of several rows, the first alternate is then the furthest from your finger.

On: the first alternate is on the row nearest the key, and the rest climb away from it. This is what most stock keyboards do, and it is a shorter reach on a key with many alternates. A popup of one row looks the same either way.

title: Order of the alternates
name: keypress_alternates_order_title
description: Which group comes first in a letter's popup
help: A letter's popup can hold three kinds of character: the alternates the layout itself puts under the key, the accents added by All accents and Native letters first, and the capital or shifted form added by Shifted letter on press and hold. Drag the groups into the order you want. Inside each group the order stays as it was. The first entry is the one a hold and release types, so the group you reach for most belongs at the top. The default is the layout's own, then the accents, then the capital.

title: Press and hold delay
name: keypress_long_press_delay_title
description: How long you hold a key before the alternate characters appear
help: This is how long you hold a key before its alternate characters appear. The alternates are accents, digits and symbols. A lower value is faster, but the popup opens by accident more easily.

title: Delete repeat interval
name: keypress_delete_repeat_title
description: How fast delete repeats while you hold it
help: While you hold delete, it repeats at this interval. Lower values delete faster.

title: Holding delete clears words
name: keypress_hold_words_title
description: A held delete key takes whole words, not letters
help:
Hold delete and, once it starts to repeat, it takes one whole word at a time instead of one letter. A single press still deletes one letter, so nothing you do quickly changes.

This works on the forward delete key as well. Each key clears the way it points: backspace takes the words before the cursor, and forward delete takes the words after it.

Word clearing has its own speed, below, because it is much faster than letter clearing.

title: Word delete interval
name: keypress_word_delete_repeat_title
description: How fast a held delete key clears words
help: While you hold delete and it clears words, it takes one word at this interval. It is slower than the letter interval above on purpose, because one word is a much bigger step. Lower values clear faster.

title: Space repeat interval
name: keypress_space_repeat_title
description: How fast space repeats while you hold it
help: While you hold the space bar, it repeats at this interval. Space has its own value because a run of spaces is harder to correct than a run of deletes. Use a higher value here to make it slower.

title: Repeating key interval
name: keypress_custom_repeat_title
description: How fast a key you set to repeat fires while you hold it
help: This is the speed of the keys you turned Repeat while held on for in the key layout editor, such as a row of arrow keys. Delete and space keep their own speeds above. Lower values repeat faster.

title: Caps lock double press
name: keypress_caps_lock_title
description: How fast a second press of shift turns on caps lock
help: Two presses of shift inside this time turn on caps lock. A shorter time makes caps lock faster, but it starts by accident more easily. A longer time accepts a slower double press. The default is 350 ms.

title: Key sound
name: hardware_sound_key_title
description: Play a sound on every key press

title: Sound volume
name: hardware_sound_volume_title
description: Relative to the media volume of your device

title: Key press haptics
name: keypress_haptics_title
description: Vibrate on each key press
help: A short vibration confirms each key press. This includes each step of the cursor movement on the spacebar. You can change the style and the strength below.

title: Haptic strength
name: keypress_haptic_strength_title
description: Vibration length for each key press
help: This is the length of the vibration pulse in milliseconds. Longer pulses feel stronger on most devices.

title: Haptic intensity
name: keypress_haptic_intensity_title
description: Vibration amplitude for each key press
help:
This sets how hard the keyboard drives the vibration motor, from 1 to 255.

For Sharp it scales the hardware click primitive. The length stays fixed and only the strength changes.

For Custom it works only on devices whose vibration motor supports amplitude control. On other devices only the duration above has an effect.

The system "Touch feedback" vibration setting also scales the final strength.

title: Press and hold haptics
name: keypress_long_press_haptics_title
description: Vibrate when a press and hold starts
help:
The keyboard vibrates a second time when a press and hold starts. This happens when the popup of alternate characters opens, or when a press and hold action runs. It tells your finger that it can lift.

Delete and space do not change. Their key repeat already vibrates on each repeat.

title: Press and hold release haptics
name: keypress_long_press_release_title
description: Vibrate on release after a press and hold
help: The keyboard vibrates again when you lift your finger at the end of a press and hold. This completes the press, hold and release loop. It is off by default. Some users find a third vibration too much.

title: Cursor movement haptics
name: keypress_cursor_haptics_title
description: Vibrate for each step when you move the cursor with the spacebar
help: The keyboard vibrates one time for each character that the cursor moves when you slide on the spacebar or use the volume keys. Turn this off to move the cursor without vibration. The keys continue to vibrate when you press them.

title: Vibrate on space
name: keypress_vibrate_space_title
description: Vibrate when you press the spacebar
help: Turn this off to stop the vibration of the spacebar only. Every other key continues to vibrate. This helps if the long spacebar feels heavy under your thumb. The key press sound still plays if it is on. This setting is on by default.

title: Vibrate on delete swipe
name: keypress_vibrate_delete_swipe_title
description: Vibrate for each word that a backspace swipe deletes
help: When you swipe left on the backspace key, the keyboard deletes word by word and vibrates for each word. Turn this off to delete a sentence with one smooth pull and no vibration. A plain press on backspace does not change. This setting is on by default.

title: Vibrate on key repeat
name: keypress_vibrate_repeat_title
description: Vibrate on each repeat while you hold a key
help: When you hold backspace or space, the key repeats. By default each repeat vibrates. Turn this off to vibrate on the first press only. The repeats still click if "Click on key repeat" is on. This setting is on by default.

title: Mute haptics in Do Not Disturb
name: keypress_dnd_mute_title
description: Stop all keyboard vibration while Do Not Disturb is on
help: By default the keyboard continues to vibrate in Do Not Disturb. Do Not Disturb applies to notifications, not to touch feedback. Turn this on to make the keyboard fully silent while Do Not Disturb is on. This setting is off by default.

title: Key popup
name: keypress_popup_title
description: Show a character bubble above the pressed key
help: While you hold a key, its character floats in a bubble above your finger. This lets you see the key that you pressed.

title: Popup on number pads
name: keypress_popup_numeric_title
description: Also show the bubble on number, phone, and date fields
help:
Number, phone, and date and time fields use a keypad. The floating character adds little there. Over a PIN it shows each digit large enough for another person to read it.

Turn this off to hide the bubble on those keypads. Normal text fields do not change.

title: Minimum popup duration
name: keypress_popup_min_duration_title
description: How long the bubble stays visible after a quick press
help: On a quick press the keyboard releases the key almost at once, so the bubble can be a flicker that you cannot see. The bubble stays after the release until it has been visible for this time. A value of 0 hides it the moment that you lift your finger.

title: Maximum popup duration
name: keypress_popup_max_duration_title
description: A limit that hides a bubble left on screen by lag
help:
The bubble normally disappears when you lift your finger. If the keyboard lags, most often as it inserts a new line, it can miss the release and the bubble stays on screen.

This is the hard limit on the life of the bubble, measured from the press. After this time the bubble always hides.

Unlike the minimum, this is not about feel. It exists only to recover from a lost release, so keep it high unless you still see a bubble that stays.

title: Popup on key
name: keypress_popup_on_key_title
description: Grow the bubble upward from the pressed key itself
help:
On: the bubble sits on the key that you press and stretches upward. It is as wide as the key, with a large character near its top. This is the look of a stock keyboard.

Off: a small bubble floats above your fingertip, with a gap.

title: Popup font size
name: keypress_popup_font_size_title
description: Text size in the preview bubble and the alternate keys
help: This multiplies the text size inside the character bubble that appears while you press a key, and in the popup of alternate keys. The size of the key labels does not change.

title: Popup height
name: keypress_popup_height_title
description: Height of the key preview bubble
help:
This is the height of the character bubble. With "Popup on key" turned on, the keyboard measures it from the bottom of the key that you press. A bubble taller than the key goes above it and stays visible past your finger.

Each of the two bubble styles keeps its own height, because a floating bubble starts above the key and needs less of it. Turn "Popup on key" on or off, and this slider shows the height of that style.

title: Popup distance above key
name: keypress_popup_offset_y_title
description: How far the floating bubble sits above the key
help:
The floating bubble sits above the key that you press. If your finger covers it, raise this distance until you can read it.

This applies only while "Popup on key" is off. The on-key bubble grows out of the key itself, so it has no distance to set. Use "Popup height" for that style.

title: Popup sideways shift
name: keypress_popup_offset_x_title
description: Move the floating bubble left or right of the key
help:
Your hand covers one side of the key more than the other. Move the bubble away from that side and you can read it without moving your hand.

A negative value moves the bubble to the left. A positive value moves it to the right. Near the edge of the keyboard the bubble stops at the edge.

title: Popup color
name: keypress_popup_background_title
description: Background of the key preview bubble
help:
By default the bubble takes its color from the keyboard theme. Pick a color here and the bubble uses it instead. Reset the row to follow the theme again.

This is only the preview bubble. The alternate keys, the language list and the menus in the panels keep the color of the theme.

title: Popup text color
name: keypress_popup_text_color_title
description: Color of the character inside the bubble
help:
By default the character takes its color from the keyboard theme. Pick a color here and the character uses it instead. Reset the row to follow the theme again.

This is only the preview bubble, as with the popup color above.

title: Popup shape
name: keypress_popup_shape_title
description: Outline of every popup, from a square to a circle
help:
This is the outline of every popup that the keyboard draws: the character bubble, the alternate keys, the language list and the menus in the panels. Only the rounded and the cut shapes follow the corner radius below. The others size their corners from the popup itself.

A theme can carry its own shape. When it does, the theme wins over this setting.

title: Popup corner radius
name: keypress_popup_radius_title
description: How round the corners of a popup are
help:
This is the corner radius of every popup. A value of 0 gives square corners. A high value makes the corners fully round.

Only the rounded and the cut popup shapes use this value. A theme can carry its own radius, and it wins over this setting.

title: Press and hold hints
name: keypress_long_press_hints_title
description: Show the alternate character of each key in its corner
help: A small label in the top right corner of each key shows its first press and hold character. This is the digit, symbol or accent at the start of the popup. Keys that run a clipboard shortcut below show no hint.

title: All accents on press and hold
name: keypress_all_accents_title
description: Fill the popup of every letter with its full set of accents
help:
This adds the complete set of accents for each Latin letter (à á â ä ã å ā …) to its press and hold popup. The keyboard keeps the characters that the layout already lists.

This setting is off by default. The built-in popups are short on purpose, and the full set has many characters. It applies to letters only.

title: Your language's letters first
name: keypress_native_letters_title
description: Put letters such as ü ahead of the number in the popup
help:
Most letter keys start their press and hold popup with a number or a symbol, such as 7 on u. With this on, the letters of the language you are typing move in front of it. In German, a hold on u then types ü, and ü is the small character in the corner of the key. The number stays in the popup, right after them.

The keyboard knows which letters belong to each language, so accents that your language does not use stay where they were. English uses no accented letters, so its keys do not change. This setting is on by default.

title: Shifted letter on press and hold
name: keypress_shifted_popup_title
description: Add what each key types under shift to its popup
help:
This adds the character each key types under shift to the end of its press and hold popup. In Latin scripts that is the capital letter. In scripts with no capitals, such as Arabic or Devanagari, it is the other letter or mark on that key, so you can reach it without pressing shift. Layouts that draw their shifted keys on a page of their own, which includes most imported Keyman keyboards, take them from that page. A key that already lists it is left alone.

It also pairs with the swipe from the ?123 and ABC keys: that gesture types one key from another layer, and the shift key is on the layer your finger has left. This setting is off by default.

title: Press and hold ?123 for the number pad
name: keypress_symbols_numpad_title
description: Press and hold the symbols key to open the number pad
help: Normally the ?123 key only changes to the symbol layer. With this setting on, hold it to open the number pad panel over any field. You get a full number pad without leaving the current text box. A quick press still changes the layer.

title: Press and hold enter for emoji
name: keypress_enter_emoji_title
description: Open the emoji panel from the enter key's popup
help:
With this setting on, holding the enter key opens a popup with an emoji entry at the front. With Choose without lifting on, a plain press and hold opens the emoji panel as soon as you lift your finger. A quick press still does what enter always does.

In a chat or search box, the same popup also has the line break that the Send or Search key replaces. Slide to it to use it. This setting is off by default.

title: Currency keys
name: keypress_currency_keys_title
help: These are the characters in the press and hold popup of the $ key, in order. Put your own currency first. Separate the characters with spaces. Keep the default (৳ € £ ¥ ₹ ₿), or clear the field to restore the built-in set.

title: Ctrl shortcuts as raw key events
name: keypress_ctrl_raw_title
description: For terminals. Off means that Ctrl+A, C, V and X use the clipboard
help:
A Ctrl key on a custom layout normally runs A, C, V and X through the clipboard actions of Android. Those work everywhere, including web pages and apps built with Compose.

A terminal needs the raw key event instead. There Ctrl+C means interrupt, not copy. The keyboard cannot tell the two apart, so this is a setting and not a guess.

title: Hold shortcuts
name: keypress_hold_actions_title
description: Edit actions in the press and hold popup of a letter key
help: Each action you pick goes into the press and hold popup of its key, after the accents that the key already has. Copy and cut take the selection, or all the text if you select nothing. Undo and redo send the same shortcuts as the toolbar tools. Choose the keys under Shortcut keys. To run the action with a plain press and hold instead, turn on Action first.

title: Action first
name: keypress_hold_action_first_title
description: Press and hold runs the action instead of showing the accents
help: The action usually sits at the end of the popup, so a plain press and hold gives you the first accent. With this on it moves to the front, and a press and hold on one of the shortcut keys runs the action straight away. The accents are still there: keep your finger down and slide onto the one you want. This needs Hold to select, under Alternate keys.

title: Slide from 🌐 for shortcuts
name: keypress_globe_drag_title
description: Press 🌐 and slide onto C to copy, V to paste
help: Put your finger on the 🌐 key, slide it onto a shortcut key and lift: onto A selects all, C copies, V pastes, X cuts, Z undoes and Y redoes. These are the same keys and the same actions as the hold shortcuts, and you can change the keys under Shortcut keys. This works when the hold shortcuts are off too. Lift anywhere else and nothing happens. Slide back onto 🌐 to change the language as a tap does. If you hold 🌐 still until the language list opens, the slide is for the list. This setting is off by default.

title: Auto theme
name: theme_auto_title
description: Use a light theme in the day and a dark theme at night

title: Change the theme
name: theme_shuffle_interval_title
description: How often a random half selects a new theme

title: Change the theme now
name: theme_shuffle_now_title
description: Select a new theme from your sets

title: Import an icon pack
name: plugins_icons_import_title
description: Opens a .wmicons file that a person shared

title: Reset all icons
name: plugins_icons_reset_title
description: This turns the pack off and deletes every single-icon change. The app keeps the installed packs.

title: Key corner radius
name: appearance_key_corner_radius_title
description: How round the corners of the keys are
help: 0 gives square keys. 28 gives keys with a full pill shape.

title: Key label font size
name: appearance_key_label_size_title
description: Scale of the labels on the keys
help: This changes the size of every label on the keys. The popup bubbles have their own font size under Key press → Key popup.

title: Key hint font size
name: appearance_key_hint_size_title
description: Scale of the small hint character in the corner of each key
help: This changes the size of the small hint that the keyboard prints in the corner of a key. The keyboard shows the hint when "Press and hold hints" is on. Larger values make the hints easier to read. The default is ×1.00.

title: Key hint position
name: appearance_key_hint_offset_title
description: Distance of the corner hint from the top edge of the key
help: At 0 dp the hint touches the top edge of the key. Larger values move the hint down, nearer to the label. The default is 1 dp.

title: Reset pinned tools
name: home_reset_pinned_tools_title
description: Restore the default toolbar tools

title: Show the toolbar
name: appearance_toolbar_show_title
description: The strip above the keys that holds the suggestions and the tools
help: The toolbar is the row above the keys. It shows the word suggestions while you type. At other times it shows your pinned tools, such as emoji, clipboard and cursor keys. Turn it off to give its height to the keys. The app asks you to confirm, because this also hides the suggestions and every tool.

title: Where the tools go
name: appearance_toolbar_placement_title
description: Share the suggestion strip, or use a row above it
help: With "The strip", the tools and the suggestions share one row. The tools rest there, the suggestions take the row while you type, and the arrow button changes between them. This costs no height. With "A button", the arrow button opens a row of tools above the suggestions, and the button closes it again. With "Always", that row of tools stays open. Both of the last two keep the tools in reach while you type, and both use the height of one more row.

title: Suggestion strip
name: appearance_toolbar_show_strip_title
description: Keep the suggestion row above the tools row
help: Turn this off to remove the suggestion row and keep only the row of tools. The keyboard gets one row shorter. Useful if you have turned suggestions off and the row sits empty. Everything else that appears in that row goes too: the paste chip for your last copy, one-time codes, snippet offers and other chips. Voice typing's compact bar still shows there while you dictate.

title: Swipe down to hide
name: appearance_toolbar_swipe_down_title
description: Swipe down on the toolbar to close the keyboard
help: When this is on, a swipe down anywhere on the toolbar closes the keyboard. It is off by default, so the gesture does not start while you scroll or rearrange the toolbar. To move a tool you press and hold it, so that gesture does not close the keyboard.

title: Rearrange by dragging
name: appearance_toolbar_drag_title
description: Press and hold a tool on the toolbar, then drag it to a new place
help: When this is on, a press and hold that moves picks the tool up so you can drop it elsewhere on the toolbar. When it is off, a press and hold that moves stays a press and hold, and the toolbox is where you rearrange the toolbar. Turn it off if a hold keeps turning into a drag by accident.

title: Only the toolbar with a hardware keyboard
name: appearance_toolbar_hardware_only_title
description: When a hardware keyboard is connected, show only the toolbar
help: When you connect a Bluetooth keyboard or a dock keyboard, the on-screen keys go away and only the toolbar stays. Emoji, clipboard and the other tools stay one press away while you type on the hardware keyboard. This setting is off by default.

title: Reverse the order for right-to-left languages
name: appearance_toolbar_rtl_title
description: Mirror the whole toolbar when you type a right-to-left script
help: For right-to-left scripts, such as Arabic, Hebrew and Persian, the whole toolbar goes from right to left, so it follows the text: the toolbox button moves to the right edge and the pinned tools run back from it. This setting is off by default, so that switching between a left-to-right and a right-to-left language leaves the tools where your fingers expect them. The toolbox grid does not change either way.

title: Tool layout
name: appearance_toolbar_fit_title
description: How the pinned tools share the toolbar
help: Fixed size keeps the tools at one size on the left. Spread out shares the full width of the toolbar between them, like the word suggestions do. Scroll keeps each tool at a comfortable size when you pin more than fit, and lets you swipe through them. You select the tools on the toolbar from the keyboard: open the toolbox with the grid button, then press and hold a tool and drag it between the toolbar and the toolbox. With Scroll, change the order from the toolbox, because a drag inside a toolbar that scrolls is difficult.

title: Toolbar top padding
name: appearance_toolbar_padding_top_title
description: Space above the tools and the suggestions
help: This adds space between the top edge of the keyboard and the toolbar. The default is 4 dp. The toolbar and the keyboard get taller by the same amount.

title: Toolbar bottom padding
name: appearance_toolbar_padding_bottom_title
description: Space between the toolbar and the keys
help: This adds space between the toolbar and the first row of keys. The default is 0 dp. The toolbar and the keyboard get taller by the same amount.

title: Hide the toolbar and the clipboard on the lock screen
name: appearance_toolbar_lock_title
description: Hide the top strip and block the clipboard while your device is locked
help: The keyboard opens over your lock screen when you answer a notification or use a search box there. This setting then hides the full top strip and blocks the clipboard panel. The strip holds the word suggestions and every pinned tool, so the clipboard tool and its paste chip also go. Copied text such as one-time codes and passwords stays off a screen that anyone can wake. This setting is off by default. When your device is unlocked, the keyboard does not change.

title: Tool labels
name: appearance_toolbar_labels_title
description: Show the name of each tool below its icon on the toolbar
help: The keyboard draws a small name below every pinned tool. Increase the toolbar height to give the labels space.

title: Label text size
name: appearance_toolbar_label_size_title
description: Font size of the tool labels on the toolbar

title: Suggestion text size
name: appearance_suggestion_text_size_title
description: How large the words in the suggestion strip are
help: Key labels have their own size setting and the suggestions above them did not, so large keys could still come with small suggestions. This also sizes the candidate row for Chinese, Japanese and Cantonese input, since it is the same row in a different mode. This setting is 100% by default.

title: Suggestion spacing
name: appearance_suggestion_spacing_title
description: The gap on each side of a word in the suggestion strip
help: Lower it to fit more of a long word before it has to shrink, or to pack more suggestions onto a narrow screen. Raise it to keep neighbouring words from reading as one when the strip scrolls. This setting is 6 dp by default.

title: Autocorrect word color
name: appearance_suggestion_primary_color_title
description: Color of the word that autocorrect will put in for a space
help: The strip draws its first suggestion in bold. Pick a color here and that word takes the color only when autocorrect has decided to put it in for you when you type a space. A bold word without the color is the top suggestion, and a space keeps what you typed. The other suggestions keep the theme color. Reset the row to follow the theme again.

title: Tool circle radius
name: appearance_tool_circle_title
description: How round the circle behind each toolbar tool is
help: 20 draws a full circle behind every tool icon, like Gboard. Smaller values give rounded squares. 0 removes the background and leaves only the icons.

title: Tool background shape
name: appearance_tool_shape_title
description: Outline of the shape behind each toolbar tool

title: Tool background width
name: appearance_tool_width_title
description: Width of the shape behind each toolbar tool
help: 38 keeps the classic circle. Wider values stretch it into a pill, like Gboard. The background only shows when the tool circle radius is above 0. Pairs well with the scrollable toolbar.

title: Tool icon size
name: appearance_tool_icon_size_title
description: Size of the icon inside each tool button
help: Applies to the toolbar and the toolbox grid. The buttons keep their size, so the same number of tools still fit. 22 is the default.

title: Reset toolbar
name: appearance_toolbar_reset_title
description: Put every setting on this screen back to its default

title: Toolbox layout
name: appearance_toolbox_layout_title
description: How the toolbox draws its tools
help: Icons is a grid. It shows a round icon for each tool with the name below it. Pills gives each tool a wide row with round ends. The icon is on the left and the name is beside it. An arrow on the right marks the tools that open something, such as Themes and Clipboard. The other tools do their work immediately, such as Flashlight and Undo. Fewer tools fit on the screen, but you can read every name.

title: Toolbox grid size
name: appearance_toolbox_columns_title
description: Tools in each row of the toolbox grid
help: The toolbox is the grid behind the grid button on the toolbar. Fewer tools in a row makes each tool larger and easier to press. More tools in a row shows more tools without a scroll.

title: Pills per row
name: appearance_toolbox_pill_columns_title
description: How many tool pills go side by side
help: The default is two. One gives every tool the full width, which is good for long names and large text. Three works only in landscape or on a tablet. On a smaller screen the names get cut.

title: Fill the pills with the tool color
name: appearance_toolbox_pill_filled_title
description: Color the full pill and not only its icon
help: When this is off, each pill keeps the background of the theme and only the icon shows the color of the tool. When it is on, the pill gets that color. The icon and the name change to a color that you can read on it: white on most colors, almost black on pale colors. This needs "Colorful tool icons" (Settings → Tools) to be on. With that setting off, there is no color to fill the pill with.

title: Swipe the toolbox in pages
name: appearance_toolbox_paginate_title
description: Fixed pages that you swipe sideways, and not one grid that scrolls
help: When this is off, the toolbox is one grid that scrolls up and down. When it is on, the toolbox becomes pages that you swipe between. Dots below the grid show your position. Every tool then keeps the same place, so you can find it from memory. You can drag a tool to a new position inside the page that you see.

title: Tools per page
name: appearance_toolbox_page_size_title
description: How many tools each toolbox page holds
help: Select a multiple of your row size to fill the last row of every page. If you select more tools than the panel can show, the page scrolls as well as swipes.

title: Reset toolbox order
name: appearance_reset_toolbox_order_title
description: Put the tools in the toolbox grid back in their original order

title: Toolbox label size
name: appearance_toolbox_label_size_title
description: The name under each tool in the full tool panel
help: By default these follow the toolbar label size, so the two agree. Set a size here to make the toolbox names larger or smaller on their own. This setting follows the toolbar by default.

title: Reset toolbox
name: appearance_toolbox_reset_title
description: Put every setting on this screen back to its default

title: Rotate the background
name: photo_rotation_on_title
description: Turn it off to keep the photo that is up now

title: Change the photo now
name: photo_rotation_shuffle_title
description: Go to the next photo

title: Photo collection
name: photo_rotation_source_saved_title
description: The photos you added yourself

title: Online photos
name: photo_rotation_source_online_title
description: New photos from Unsplash and Pexels

title: Subjects
name: photo_rotation_topics_title
description: Optional

title: Safe photos only
name: photo_rotation_safe_title
description: Tell the service to remove adult photos

title: Wide photos only
name: photo_rotation_wide_title
description: A keyboard is wide and short, so wide photos fit better

title: Use mobile data
name: photo_rotation_metered_title
description: Get photos when there is no Wi-Fi

title: Photos to keep ready
name: photo_rotation_pool_title
help: More photos make the background repeat less frequently, but the app uses more storage. The app keeps the photos on the device, so the background changes also when there is no network.

title: Delete the photos that the app got
name: photo_rotation_delete_downloads_title
description: The app will get a new set at the next change

title: Add from this device
name: photo_add_device_title
description: The app copies each photo, so it stays available

title: Symbols on shift
name: layout_number_row_shift_symbols_title
description: Press and hold shift to change the digit row to symbols
help: While you hold shift on the letter layout, the number row shows the fill row of the symbol layer (= \\ < > [ ] { } | ~) instead of the digits. You reach those symbols with one shift, and you do not change to the symbols layer. On the second symbols layer, the number row already shows more arrow and comparison symbols.

title: Number row in symbols
name: layout_number_row_in_symbols_title
description: Keep the digit row on the ?123 symbols layer too
help: The digit row stays in place when you change to the symbols layer. This is the default. Turn it off to drop the digits from the ?123 layer and keep them on the letters, where the number row is already showing them. The symbols keep their bracket and maths row, so nothing but the digits goes, and the keyboard is one row shorter on the symbols layer.

title: Arrow keys row
name: layout_arrow_row_title
description: Show left, up, down and right keys under the keyboard
help: The keyboard adds a row of four arrow keys under the spacebar, so you can move the cursor without the toolbar or a drag on the spacebar. Hold an arrow to keep moving. The row is as tall as the number row, and the keyboard grows by that much.

title: Arrow order
name: layout_arrow_row_order_title
description: Drag the handles to put the arrows in the order you want
help: The keys appear on the row from left to right in the order of this list.

title: Go back to the letters
name: layout_symbols_return_title
description: Leave ?123 after you type one of these characters
help: You change to ?123 for one full stop or one question mark, and the keyboard changes back to the letters after it. Turn this off to stay on the symbols layer until you press ABC. The emoji panel has the same setting.

title: Characters that go back
name: layout_symbols_return_chars_title
help: Type the characters that send the keyboard back to the letters. Spaces between them are optional. An empty box uses the default characters ! ? . , ; and :. Digits are not in the default set, because you usually type more than one digit at a time.

title: Go back after a space
name: layout_symbols_return_space_title
description: Leave ?123 when you press the spacebar
help: You type a number or a symbol on ?123, press space, and the keyboard changes back to the letters for the next word. Turn this off to stay on the symbols layer, for example to type a phone number with spaces in it. This works on its own, with or without Go back to the letters.

title: Type native digits in
name: layout_numeral_scope_title
description: Where the keyboard types the native digits
help: You select the digit glyphs for each language under Languages → the language → Numerals. This setting controls where the keyboard also types those glyphs. "Text fields" is the default. It types 0-9 in number, phone, date and time fields, which keeps them machine-readable. In all other fields it types the native digits. "Everywhere" types the native digits in those fields too. "Display only" shows the glyphs on the keys but always types 0-9.

title: Key layouts
name: langemoji_lang_keymaps_title
description: Edit, add and delete layouts

title: Comma key opens emoji
name: layout_comma_emoji_title
description: Replace the comma key with an emoji key
help: The comma key on the bottom row becomes an emoji key, and the comma moves into the press and hold alternates. This also deletes the emoji tool from the toolbar, because the key replaces it. Drag the tool out of the toolbox again if you want both.

title: Press and hold enter for emoji
name: keypress_enter_emoji_title
description: Open the emoji panel from the enter key's popup
help:
With this setting on, holding the enter key opens a popup with an emoji entry at the front. With Choose without lifting on, a plain press and hold opens the emoji panel as soon as you lift your finger. A quick press still does what enter always does.

In a chat or search box, the same popup also has the line break that the Send or Search key replaces. Slide to it to use it. This setting is off by default.

title: Show the 🌐 key
name: layout_show_globe_title
description: Turn off to give its space to the spacebar
help: When this is off, the 🌐 key is not on the bottom row of any layout. If "Emoji key instead of 🌐" is on, the emoji key in that position goes too. The spacebar gets the space. You can still change the language from the spacebar. Set a swipe to "Language" under Typing → Gestures. A short swipe does this by default.

title: 🌐 goes back to the last language
name: layout_globe_recent_title
description: Tap quickly to go further back
help: When this is on, one tap on the 🌐 key goes back to the layout you used before this one, and the next tap comes back again. This is useful with many languages when you only type two or three of them at a time. Tap several times quickly to go further back, most recently used first. A list shows where you are. When this is off, each tap goes to the next layout in your switch order. This also changes the language key on a physical keyboard. This setting is off by default.

title: Ignore 🌐 right after typing
name: layout_globe_guard_title
description: A tap on 🌐 just after a letter does nothing
help: The 🌐 key is next to the spacebar and the comma, so a fast thumb can hit it by mistake in the middle of a word and change the language. Set a time here and a tap on 🌐 that comes sooner than this after a typed key does nothing. A tap after a pause changes the language as usual, and so do quick taps one after the other on 🌐 itself. Press and hold 🌐 to open the language list at any time. Letters, space, backspace and enter count as typing. Shift and the mode keys do not. This setting is off by default.

title: Emoji key instead of 🌐
name: layout_globe_emoji_title
description: Replace the language key with an emoji key
help: The 🌐 key on the bottom row opens the emoji panel and does not change the language. You can still change the language from the spacebar. Set a swipe to "Language" under Typing → Gestures. A short swipe does this by default. Turn this off to get the 🌐 key back.

title: Swap the comma and 🌐 keys
name: layout_swap_comma_globe_title
description: Put the comma next to the spacebar
help: The two keys on each side of the spacebar change places. If one of them is an emoji key, it moves to the outer position and the comma stays next to the spacebar. Turn this off to get the usual order.

title: Keep the 🌐 key in one place
name: layout_globe_in_one_place_title
description: The same place on every layout, beside the spacebar
help: Some layouts put the 🌐 key in a different place, for example at the far left, or directly after the ?123 key. This moves it to the place the built-in layouts use, so your thumb finds it in the same place in every language. The keys to its left get wider or narrower to make room, and the spacebar changes to fit. A layout where that would make keys too small is left as it is, and so is a second layout you open from a key. Turn this off to see every layout as its author made it.

title: Import a layout
name: layout_editor_import_title
description: Opens a .wmlayout.json file that someone shared

title: Panel layouts
name: panel_layouts_title
description: The panels every layout uses unless it has a panel grid of its own. Each layout's editor has a tab for every panel.

title: Add tablet keys automatically
name: layout_editor_tablet_expand_title
description: On a tablet, add tab, backslash, caps lock, a second shift and the arrow keys around this layout

title: Number row
name: layout_number_row_title
description: Show a row of digits above the letters
help: The keyboard adds a row of digits from 1 to 0 above the letter keys, so you do not press and hold for a digit. The digits on the press and hold of the top letter row are not available while this is on. The keyboard becomes one row taller.

title: Number row height
name: layout_number_row_height_title
description: The height of the digit row, separate from the letter keys
help: A short digit row keeps fast access to the numbers. It adds less height to the keyboard than a full row.

title: Key height
name: layout_key_height_title
description: The height of each key row, which sets the total keyboard height
help: Tall keys are easier to press, but the keyboard covers more of the screen. The emoji, clipboard and snippet panels change size with this value too.

title: Bottom row height
name: layout_bottom_row_height_title
description: The height of the space and enter row on its own
help: The bottom row holds the spacebar and enter. Give it a height that is taller or shorter than the letter keys, to get a larger spacebar without a taller keyboard. "Follow keys" is the default and keeps the bottom row the same height as the other rows. Custom layouts that set their own row heights ignore this setting.

title: Left padding
name: layout_side_padding_left_title
description: Move the left edge of the keyboard toward the centre
help: The keyboard keeps this much of the screen width clear on the left. The keys move toward the middle for thumb reach, and the keyboard does not dock to one edge as one-handed mode does. The default is 0 percent. This setting applies on top of the keyboard width above.

title: Right padding
name: layout_side_padding_right_title
description: Move the right edge of the keyboard toward the centre
help: The keyboard keeps this much of the screen width clear on the right. Set it to the same value as the left padding for an even margin, or to a different one to shift the keys toward the hand you type with. The default is 0 percent.

title: Key spacing
name: layout_key_spacing_title
description: The gap between the keys
help: This changes the space around each key. A larger value moves the keys apart and makes the keyboard a little taller, because the gap is part of each row. A smaller value moves the keys closer together. The default is 100 percent.

title: Extend edge keys into the gaps
name: layout_extend_edge_keys_title
description: A tap in the blank space at the end of a short row types the nearest key
help: Some rows are shorter than the keyboard, for example the A to L row of QWERTY. They have blank space at the left and right ends. With this setting on, a tap in that space types the key at that end of the row, so a tap to the left of A types A. The keys do not change size or position. Only the area that you can tap gets larger. This setting is on by default.

title: Keyboard scale
name: layout_keyboard_scale_title
description: Make the whole keyboard smaller or larger on this screen

title: Bottom padding
name: layout_bottom_padding_title
description: More space below the keys, above the navigation bar
help: The whole keyboard moves up, away from the bottom edge and the gesture navigation bar. Increase it if the bottom row is too near the edge of the screen, or if you start the system navigation by mistake.

title: Round top corners
name: layout_board_corner_top_title
description: Cut round corners into the top of the keyboard

title: Round bottom corners
name: layout_board_corner_bottom_title
description: Cut round corners into the bottom of the keyboard

title: Keyboard width
name: layout_keyboard_width_title
description: Make the keyboard narrower
help: Below 100 percent the keyboard does not fill the whole screen. Select the edge that it sits at below. This helps on very wide screens. One-handed mode below is a quick preset, and it replaces this value while it is on.

title: Keyboard position
name: layout_keyboard_position_title
description: Where the narrow keyboard sits: at the left edge, in the centre, or at the right edge.
help: Where the narrow keyboard sits: at the left edge, in the centre, or at the right edge.

title: Follow portrait again
name: layout_follow_portrait_title
description: Delete the sizes that you set for %1$s

title: One-handed mode
name: layout_one_handed_title
description: Make the keyboard smaller at one edge of the screen

title: Portrait only
name: layout_one_handed_portrait_only_title
description: Use the whole width when the phone is sideways
help: One-handed mode is one setting for both orientations, so a keyboard made small for a thumb in portrait stays small after you turn the phone, where you may want a split keyboard instead. Turn this on to keep one-handed mode in portrait and switch it off in landscape. Turn the phone back and it comes back. This setting is off by default.

title: Split keyboard
name: layout_split_title
description: Divide the keys into a left half and a right half
help: The keyboard divides each row in the middle and puts a gap between the halves, so your thumbs move less on wide screens. This helps most on tablets, foldable devices and phones in landscape. By default the keyboard also divides the spacebar between the two halves.

title: Split gap
name: layout_split_gap_title
description: The width of the gap between the halves
help: This is the gap in the centre, as a percentage of the keyboard width. A larger gap moves the halves toward the edges, but each key becomes narrower.

title: Split the spacebar
name: layout_split_spacebar_title
description: Divide the spacebar too, or keep it as one key across the gap
help: When this is on, the spacebar is divided between the two halves like every other row, and the centre of the bottom row is empty. When this is off, the spacebar stays as one key and fills the gap, so both thumbs can press it where they meet. The other keys on the bottom row stay in their halves. This setting is on by default.

title: Floating keyboard
name: layout_floating_title
description: Put the keyboard in a panel that you can move
help: The keyboard becomes a small panel that floats above the apps, and it does not dock to the bottom of the screen. Drag the pill at the top of the panel to move it. Drag the corner grip to change the size. Press the dock button to go back to the normal keyboard. Apps do not change size while the panel floats, and touches outside the panel go to the app.

title: Floating keyboard width
name: layout_floating_width_title
description: You can also drag the corner grip of the panel
help: This is the width of the floating panel. The key heights still follow the sliders above.

title: Keep the keyboard on screen
name: layout_persistent_title
description: Stay open when no text field has focus
help: After the keyboard opens, it stays on screen when the text field closes, and over apps that have no text field. This lets you send keys and keyboard shortcuts to an app, for example to set a hotkey in a notes app. To close the keyboard, press the hide key, swipe down on the toolbar, or press Back. It opens again the next time you tap a text field. The keyboard never stays on the lock screen. Works docked or floating.

title: Carry the word over
name: langemoji_lang_carry_word_title
description: Switch to a phonetic layout mid-word and the letters that you typed convert too
help: Phonetic layouts such as Avro, Hindi phonetic and Khipro spell their script with roman letters. When you notice halfway through a word that you are still on your Latin keyboard, switching language now converts the letters that you already typed instead of leaving them as they are: type "tu", switch to Avro, and the word reads তু, so "mi" after it finishes তুমি. Turn this off if you often switch language right after an English word and before typing a space, because that word is carried over as well.

title: Remember language per app
name: langemoji_lang_per_app_toggle_title
description: Open each app with the layout that you used there last
help: When you change language while you type in an app, the keyboard remembers your choice for that app. The keyboard uses that language again the next time that you type there. You can change language with the 🌐 key, a spacebar swipe or the picker. Apps where you selected no language use your last language. A field that requires Latin letters, such as a password box, still overrides this. A field that gives its own language also overrides this.

title: List languages in the Android switcher
name: langemoji_lang_os_switcher_title
description: Add each language to the input method switcher of the system
help:
The keyboard registers every layout that you turn on as an Android input method subtype. The "Choose input method" sheet of the system then lists them, and you can change between them there. Turn this off to keep language switching inside the keyboard only, with the 🌐 key, a spacebar swipe or the picker. The keyboard then gives no subtypes to the system, and the sheet lists it as "WM Keyboard" instead of as one language name.

To register a language and to make it switchable are two different things. Android lists only the languages that something turns on. Until then, Android selects them itself from the languages of your device, and it usually selects one. On Android 14 and newer, the keyboard turns them all on for you. On older versions, select them by hand in the system settings with the row below.

title: Show app name first
name: langemoji_lang_app_name_first_title
description: The label reads "WM Keyboard · <language>"
help: This puts the app name in front of the language in the label of the switcher. Android decides how it styles the label and the app name, such as which one is bold or grey. This setting changes only the label text, not that styling.

title: Select languages in the system settings
name: langemoji_lang_subtype_enabler_title
description: The list of Android. Use it only if the switcher looks wrong

title: Conjunct-aware backspace
name: languages_conjunct_backspace_title
description: Delete a whole cluster like %1$s as one unit
help: Backspace usually deletes one code point at a time. This sometimes leaves half-formed clusters on the screen. With this setting on, one press deletes the whole cluster while you type %1$s. Other languages keep their own setting.

title: Show the letter each key types
name: languages_translit_hints_row_title
description: Put the %1$s a key is about to write in its corner

title: Keep the first two words in place
name: languages_phonetic_strip_fixed_title
description: What you typed first, the %1$s word next, then suggestions
help:
Usually the first word on the strip is the word that the space bar will write, so the words move as you type.

With this on, the first two words always stay in the same place. On the left is what you typed, in English letters. Next to it is the %1$s that the phonetic rules make from it, letter for letter. The suggestions come after them. Tap the left word to write in English, or the word next to it to write the exact %1$s reading.

The space bar does not change: it writes the same word as before. That word shows in bold, and in the autocorrect word color if you set one. The strip does not put a word in the middle on this layout, so that the left word is always first.

title: Suggestions after them
name: languages_phonetic_strip_source_title
description: Which language fills the rest of the strip

title: Avro candidate list
name: languages_phonetic_candidates_title
description: The words desktop Avro shows under the word you type
help:
Desktop Avro shows a short list under the word you type. The list is built the same way here. First comes the known spelling for what you typed, if there is one. Next come the %1$s dictionary words that sound like it, and the words made by adding an ending to one of them, such as বন্ধু + দের. The words closest to the letter-for-letter reading come first. Last is the letter-for-letter reading itself.

In the suggestion strip: the word that the space bar will write stays first, and the list follows it. Bar above the strip: the whole list goes in a row of its own above the strip, and you can scroll through it. The row stays while the layout is on, so the keyboard does not change height between words.

The space bar writes the same word with all three choices.

title: Full guide
name: languages_phonetic_guide_title
description: Every rule with examples, on the WM Keyboard website

title: Allow ANSI output
name: languages_ansi_allowed_title
description: An ANSI button on the Bengali layouts writes Bijoy-style text, so আ comes out as Av
help:
ANSI is how Bengali was written before Unicode, in Bijoy and in fonts like SutonnyMJ: each Bengali letter is stored as a Latin character, and the font draws it as Bengali. Some design software and older documents still need it.

With this on, every Bengali layout gets an ANSI button beside the suggestions. Tap it and what you type goes into the text box as ANSI, so আমার সোনার বাংলা becomes Avgvi †mvbvi evsjv. Tap it again for Unicode.

The word you are typing shows as Unicode until you finish it. ANSI text only reads as Bengali in an ANSI font, so keep the button off everywhere else.

title: ANSI version
name: languages_ansi_version_title
description: Pick the one your ANSI font is made for
help: The ANSI fonts do not all put the letters in the same places, so there are three versions. Version 2 is the common one, used by SutonnyMJ and most Bijoy fonts. If the text comes out as the wrong letters in your font, try another version.

title: Fancy style
name: languages_fancy_style_row_title
description: The lettering the fancy keyboard types. Also switchable from the strip over the keys.

title: Only tone real syllables
name: languages_vietnamese_strict_tones_title
description: A tone key is a letter unless the word is one the language spells
help: Telex and VNI mark a tone whenever the vowels allow it, so typing fas gives fá even though f is not a Vietnamese onset and there is no word there. With this on, a tone key that would land on something that is not a word is typed as the letter it is drawn as instead, and only a syllable the language actually spells takes a tone. mix is still mĩ, because that is a word.

title: Fill in left-out marks
name: languages_vietnamese_restore_marks_title
description: With the Vietnamese word list, tieng becomes tiếng when it can only be one word
help: Telex and VNI type only the marks you spell. With this on, a word you finish without one of its marks gets it from the Vietnamese word list, but only when the list has one way to read it: tieng becomes tiếng and duong becomes đường. A word the list already has is never changed, and a spelling like toan, which can be toàn, toán or toản, stays as you typed it. One backspace takes the change back. This needs autocorrect on and the Vietnamese word list on the device.

title: Numeral system
name: languages_numeral_system_title
description: The digits that the number row and the keypad show while you type %1$s
help: You select the digits for %1$s: its own digits, which are %2$s, or 0-9. This applies to this language only. The keys always show the digits that you select. To set where the keyboard also types them, open Layout & size, then Numerals.

title: Custom dictionaries
name: languages_custom_dictionaries_title
description: Import your own word lists

title: Dictionaries
name: languages_dictionaries_title
help: Each item works offline after the download. The checkbox turns an item off and keeps the file. Delete removes the file from the device.

title: Traditional characters
name: languages_cjk_traditional_title
description: The keyboard converts candidates to Traditional (繁體). It converts one character at a time, so a few forms that depend on context are wrong (发 → 發 / 髮).
help: The keyboard converts each candidate from Simplified (简体) to Traditional (繁體) before it shows the candidate. The conversion reads one character at a time. A few Simplified characters have more than one Traditional form, and the keyboard always writes the more common one. 发 becomes 發, which is correct in 發展 but wrong in 頭髮. Correct those words by hand.

title: Lazy pronunciation (懶音)
name: languages_cjk_lazy_title
description: Match merged sounds: n↔l, ng↔∅, gw→g before -o, -ng↔-n, -k↔-t…

title: Match kana without marks
name: languages_cjk_loose_marks_title
description: かつこう also finds 学校 (がっこう)
help: On the Flick and Kana JIS layouts, a small kana, a ゛ or a ゜ is an extra key. With this on, a plain kana also matches those forms: か finds が, つ finds っ and づ, は finds ば and ぱ, や finds ゃ. When two words are almost equally common, the one that you typed exactly comes first. A kana that you typed with a mark is not changed, and Romaji typing is not changed.

title: Full-width space
name: languages_cjk_full_width_space_title
description: The space bar types a full-width space [　]
help: Japanese and Chinese text is spaced with the ideographic space (U+3000), which is as wide as one character. With this on, the space bar types it instead of the narrow space used between words in other languages. A space pressed while you are still typing a reading picks a candidate as before, and only a press with nothing waiting to convert types a space.

title: Jianpin (简拼)
name: languages_cjk_jianpin_title
description: Type only the first letter of a syllable: wm finds 我们, zg finds 中国
help: A letter that is not a whole syllable stands for every syllable that starts with it, so wm finds 我们 and haod finds 好的. Each letter is one syllable: hd means h… plus d…. A syllable that you type in full is matched exactly and ranks first. The letters z, c and s also cover zh, ch and sh. A Double Pinyin scheme does not use this, because every syllable is exactly two keys there.

title: Fuzzy Pinyin
name: languages_cjk_fuzzy_title
description: Match confusable sounds: zh↔z, ch↔c, sh↔s, n↔l, an↔ang, in↔ing…

title: Custom Double Pinyin scheme
name: languages_cjk_double_pinyin_custom_title
description: Set your own keys. Copy, paste, import or export the scheme, in the same format as fcitx

title: Emoji button in toolbar
name: langemoji_emoji_toolbar_title
description: Open emoji with one press from the top bar
help: The emoji button stays visible in the top bar, also while the suggestions show. The emoji panel has a tab for each category. You can search in English and Bengali, and in any language that you add a keyword pack for. Press and hold an emoji for the skin tone variants.

title: Button beside the suggestions
name: langemoji_strip_shortcut_title
description: The tool that stays in the top bar while the suggestions show

title: Full-screen emoji panel
name: langemoji_emoji_full_bleed_title
description: Hide the toolbar and move the category tabs up, next to a back button
help: The emoji panel fills the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row go away. The category tabs move into the row that they leave, next to a back button. Turn this off to keep the toolbar in reach while you select emoji.

title: Panel layout
name: panel_layout_row_title
description: Arrange the keys and the parts of this panel

title: Emoji suggestions
name: langemoji_emoji_prediction_title
description: Show emoji while you type. The word birthday suggests 🎂 🎉 🥳
help: Emoji that match appear at the end of the suggestion strip while you type. This works in English and in any language whose keywords you have. %1$s also suggests 🎂.

title: Press an emoji suggestion
name: langemoji_emoji_insert_mode_title
description: What happens to the word that you typed. Hold the suggestion for the other one
help:
"Replace word" changes the word that you typed to the emoji. If you type birthday and press 🎂, only 🎂 stays, as in Gboard. "Keep word" adds the emoji after the word: birthday 🎂.

Hold an emoji suggestion to do the other one this time. With "Replace word" selected, a hold keeps the word. With "Keep word" selected, a hold replaces it.

title: Emoji row
name: langemoji_emoji_row_title
description: A row of your own emoji, like Gboard

title: Emoji row content
name: langemoji_emoji_bar_content_title
description: Favourites always come first

title: Emoji in the row
name: langemoji_emoji_bar_count_title
description: How many fit across. A higher number packs them tighter
help: The row divides its width into this many slots and makes the emoji small enough to fit them. A higher number gives smaller emoji that are closer together. When scrolling is off, the row hides the emoji after the last slot. When scrolling is on, a swipe shows them.

title: Scroll the emoji row
name: langemoji_emoji_bar_scroll_title
description: Swipe sideways for the emoji after the visible ones
help: When this is on, and it is on by default, you can swipe the row sideways to reach the emoji after the visible ones. When this is off, the row does not move. It shows only the emoji that fit, so a sideways swipe cannot move it under your finger.

title: Emoji font
name: langemoji_emoji_font_title
description: How emoji look on the keyboard itself
help: "System" uses the emoji pack of your device. On Samsung devices that is the Samsung set. "Google" downloads Noto Color Emoji, the standard Android look, one time through the system font provider, and keeps it on your device. "Installed" uses an emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. "Custom" uses one emoji font file that you import below. The text that you send is always plain Unicode. Other apps and other devices draw it with their own emoji font.

title: Default skin tone
name: langemoji_emoji_skin_tone_title
description: For toned emoji in the panel, the suggestions and the search
help: The keyboard shows toned emoji (👍, 🙏, 🧑…) with this Fitzpatrick tone in the grid of the emoji panel, the suggestion strip and the emoji search results. It also inserts them with that tone. An emoji that you selected a tone for keeps your tone while "Override with last used" is on. The first option (✋) keeps the neutral yellow base.

title: Override with last used
name: langemoji_emoji_tone_override_title
description: Use the tone that you selected last for an emoji, not the default
help: When this is on, and it is on by default, an emoji that you already selected a tone for keeps that tone everywhere: in the panel, the suggestions and the search. You select that tone from the press and hold popup of the emoji in the panel. The emoji does not use the default above. When this is off, the default skin tone always wins.

title: Hide emoji that your device cannot show
name: langemoji_emoji_hide_unrenderable_title
description: Skip emoji that show as a blank box in the panel, the search and the suggestions
help: Older devices, and some brands, have an emoji font that is older than the newest emoji. Those emoji then show as an empty "tofu" box. This setting hides every emoji that the emoji font of your device cannot draw. To see them all, set the emoji font above to "Google" (Noto Color Emoji). You can also install a complete emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. WM Keyboard has no emoji font of its own. It uses the font that you select here.

title: Find any character by its Unicode name
name: langemoji_emoji_unicode_search_title
description: The emoji search also finds symbols, letters and marks by the words of their name
help: Type the words of a character's Unicode name in the emoji search and it appears after the emoji: em dash, copyright sign, greek small letter lambda, latin small letter a with ogonek. Every character of the Basic Multilingual Plane is covered, which is tens of thousands of letters, marks and symbols. Tapping one inserts it. This setting is off by default.

title: Grid size
name: langemoji_emoji_grid_size_title
description: How wide each cell of the emoji grid is, at least. A smaller size fits more columns
help: The emoji panel fits as many columns as its width allows, and each cell is at least this wide. A smaller size packs more emoji on one screen. A larger size spreads them out, and each one is easier to hit. When the emoji size below needs more room than this, the cells grow to fit it.

title: Emoji size
name: langemoji_emoji_size_title
description: How large the emoji panel draws each emoji
help: The size of the emoji in the grid of the emoji panel, on every tab and in the search results. The cells always keep enough room around each emoji, so a very large size can also mean fewer columns. The press and hold popup keeps its own size.

title: History tab
name: langemoji_emoji_tab_mode_title
description: What the first tab of the emoji panel shows
help: "Recent" lists emoji in the order that you used them last. "Most used" puts the emoji that you use most often first. The keyboard always keeps your favourite emoji at the start of both lists.

title: Clear recents button
name: langemoji_emoji_clear_recents_title
description: A button on the Recent tab that deletes the recents list
help: This adds a "Clear recents" button to the Recent tab of the emoji panel. It is off by default, to keep the tab clean.

title: Kaomoji and Emoticons
name: langemoji_emoji_kaomoji_title
description: Two extra tabs: ¯\\_(ツ)_/¯ and :-)
help: This adds a Kaomoji tab and an Emoticons tab at the end of the tabs of the emoji panel. Kaomoji are Japanese style faces, such as (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻. Emoticons are the Western ASCII ones, such as :-D and <3. Both tabs group them by mood. If you press one, the keyboard types it as plain text. It does not go into your emoji history.

title: Emoji descriptions
name: langemoji_emoji_long_press_name_title
description: Show the name of the emoji at the top of its press and hold popup
help: Press and hold an emoji to show its Unicode name, such as "skull and crossbones". The name appears above the favourite control and the variant controls. This helps you to see the difference between emoji that look almost the same.

title: Animated emoji
name: langemoji_emoji_animated_title
description: Send a moving version of an emoji from its press and hold popup
help: Press and hold an emoji in the emoji panel to see the moving version, and a control that sends it as an image. The images are Noto Animated Emoji by Google, under the CC BY 4.0 licence. The keyboard downloads each one from Google when you ask for it, at about 800 KB. About 880 emoji have one, and the control does not appear for the others, or in an app that accepts no images.

title: Send emoji as image
name: langemoji_emoji_sticker_title
description: Add a control that sends the emoji itself as a picture
help: Press and hold an emoji in the emoji panel to get a control that sends it as a picture, in the emoji font that you selected. This is useful when the other person has a device that draws the emoji differently, or cannot draw it at all. The keyboard draws the picture on your device and downloads nothing, except one time for the Google emoji font. The picture goes out in the same way as the stickers of the sticker tool. To change that, open Tools, then Stickers, then "Send stickers as". The control does not appear in an app that accepts no images.

title: Return to the keyboard after you insert
name: langemoji_emoji_close_after_insert_title
description: Close the panel when you insert one emoji or paste one clip
help: By default, the emoji panel and the clipboard panel stay open, so that you can select several items. Turn this on to go back to the keys directly after one emoji or one clipboard paste.

title: Switch to GIFs and stickers
name: langemoji_media_switcher_title
description: Where the emoji, GIF and sticker panels show the buttons that go between them
help: The switch has one button for each of the emoji panel, the GIF panel and the sticker panel, so that you can go from one to the next directly. It is at the same place in all three panels. "Bottom" puts it in the bottom row, between ABC and the space bar. "Top" puts it at the end of the search row. The GIF button and the sticker button show only while those tools are on. If you changed the layout of the emoji panel, the switch is where your layout puts it. To add it, use the "Emoji, GIF and sticker switch" part in the panel layout editor.

title: Open the last used panel
name: langemoji_media_remember_title
description: The emoji key opens emoji, GIFs or stickers, the same as you left them
help: When this is on, the emoji key and the emoji tool open the panel of the three that you used last. If one of the three panels is open, they close it. When this is off, the emoji key always opens the emoji panel. The keyboard forgets the last panel when it restarts.

title: Recognition engine
name: voice_engine_title
description: How the keyboard turns speech into text
help: The system recognizer is fast and shows the words while you speak, but it depends on the operating system and its languages. Offline Whisper runs fully on your device across many languages and sends no audio anywhere. It transcribes each phrase after you stop speaking. A transcription server does the same work on a computer you choose, so your phone spends less battery. The recording of each phrase goes to that server and nowhere else.

title: Voice typing view
name: voice_ui_title
description: What the microphone button opens
help: The panel gives large controls and status in the space of the keyboard. The compact bar speaks over the keys, so you can correct words as they land. The collapsed bar hides the whole keyboard behind a small pill that you can drag anywhere, and it stays until you bring the keyboard back. The panel and the compact bar have a collapse button, and the pill has an expand button, so you can switch styles without coming back to this screen.
